subject: MAP milestones: evidence delivery window vs order-form cutover
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@auroraht.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: MAP alignment: evidence delivery window & order-form cutover

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our MAP, we want to lock the procurement and legal gating so we can plan a smooth activation without a last-minute hold. Two quick asks to help sync timelines:

1) Confirm Aurora's acceptable evidence delivery window for SOC2 / DPA attestations and sample logs (we typically provide a matrix documenting which artifacts are needed and timing).
2) Confirm the latest acceptable order-form cutover date (when procurement needs the final countersigned order form to meet your internal billing/commitment cycle).

Proposal from our side:
- MSA/DPA executed and countersigned by Aurora legal: target week of Jun 7–11
- Evidence bundle delivered (SOC2 report, data flow diagram, sample audit logs): by Jun 18
- Order form countersigned: target week of Jun 21–25
- Provisioning/go-live (soft launch): week of Jul 5

Attaching an evidence matrix for Aurora to review (aurora_evidence_matrix.xlsx). If those dates are too aggressive for procurement, let us know which milestone(s) you'd like to shift.

Thanks — I’ve copied Jordan (CS) so we can coordinate the acceptance tests and Neha (Security) will jump in once legal checkpoints are clearer.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

On Fri, 29 May 2026 09:10:00 -0700 Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo yesterday...

Hi Lauren — thanks for the clear draft. A few constraints from Aurora procurement/legal:

- Procurement cycle: our purchasing committee meets on the second Tuesday of each month; with materials in by June 2 we can aim for approval the week of June 14. If docs miss that cut, the next committee is July 12.
- Legal requirements: we need an up-to-date DPA (we have a template) and an SOC2 Type II report or compensating controls summary; if Redwood can supply the SOC2 summary + a short evidence bundle by June 10, legal will have what they need for the June 14 packet.
- Order form timing: procurement prefers the fully executed order form by June 18 to hit July billing; if legal approval slips, procurement can accept a conditional countersign (order form subject to final DPA signature) but we need the dependency spelled out in the MAP.

Attachment(s): Aurora_required_evidence_list.csv (CSV) — procurement pasted a short checklist.

Proposed pragmatic path from our side:
- Redwood sends evidence summary + DPA redline by Jun 8
- Aurora legal reviews Jun 9–11
- Purchasing committee packet submitted Jun 12 for Jun 14 vote
- If all goes well, countersigned order form by Jun 18, billing effective Jul 1

If Redwood thinks getting the SOC2 summary by Jun 8 is tight, call out which artifacts you can deliver earlier (ex: architecture diagram + sample logs) so we can still get materials to the committee.

—Sam

samantha.cole@auroraht.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@auroraht.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP alignment: evidence delivery window & order-form cutover

Thanks Sam / Lauren — quick legal calibration.

Quoted for context:
> On Fri, 29 May 2026 11:22:00 -0700 Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@auroraht.com> wrote:
> > Procurement cycle: our purchasing committee meets on the second Tuesday of each month...

We want to avoid a sequencing risk where procurement signs an order form that references data-processing commitments that are not yet finalized in the DPA. Two practical options:

A) Sequential (preferred for low legal risk)
- Execute MSA + DPA first (both countersigned).
- Deliver evidence bundle and complete acceptance test window.
- Execute order form (pricing + term specifics) as confirmation of commercial commitment.

B) Conditional order-form (operationally faster, higher legal coordination)
- Procurement and customer sign the order form with an express condition: "Order becomes effective upon execution of DPA and completion of acceptance tests."
- MSA/DPA executed in parallel with procurement review; DocuSign envelope ties the signatures together.

Our recommended cadence to balance Aurora procurement dates and legal comfort:
- Redwood to deliver SOC2 summary + architecture diagram + evidence matrix by Tue Jun 8 (we can accept a short compensating-controls memo if Type II report is pending).
- Target DPA finalization and MSA countersign on Fri Jun 11. (DocuSign link below for the initial MSA + placeholder DPA.)
- If procurement requires the order form for the June 14 packet, sign a conditional order form with the clear effective-date condition; final countersign for commercial effect by Jun 25 after DPA signature.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-proposed-orderform
Attachment: aurora_evidence_matrix.xlsx (we updated the matrix with fields flagged as "required for committee" vs "nice-to-have").

If Aurora accepts the conditional order-form approach, CS (Jordan) should prepare a short acceptance-test plan that demonstrates the readiness criteria for production. Jordan / Neha — can you draft that plan (one page) for inclusion in the committee packet?

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: aurora_evidence_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
